pr_title: Fix mipmap bias behavior by refactoring how samplers are created by Material Storage.
pr_body:
Introduces a new structure to store samplers created with certain parameters instead of storing a 'custom' set of samplers. Allows viewports to correctly configure the mipmap bias and use it when rendering the scene.

This effectively fixes [#81214](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/81214) and also introduces rendering improvements for the FSR 2 PR https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/81197, which will be adapted to account for this behavior properly when this is merged.

The most obvious way to test this is that changing the mipmap bias setting at the project level or per viewport effectively did nothing before. This also fixes the issue where it was not possible to use different mipmap biases across different viewports.

The fix should work for both RenderingDevice-based renderers Forward+ and Mobile.
pr_comments: Thanks @AThousandShips for the suggestions, I forgot about the parameter rules for a bit there.
Added the change to mobile renderer as well, although originally they didn't use the 'custom' samplers in the projectors and decals.

> This also fixes the issue where it was not possible to use different mipmap biases across different viewports.

Would this make it possible to use a different mipmap bias for 2D and 3D rendering in a single viewport in the future? Right now, changing mipmap bias in a viewport affects both 2D and 3D. (Note that mipmaps are disabled by default in 2D; you need to enable them in the 2D filter property of Viewport, **and** enable the Mipmaps import option on the texture.)

This should be achievable using two viewports thanks to your PR now, but using a single viewport should reduce the performance overhead.

> Would this make it possible to use a different mipmap bias for 2D and 3D rendering in a single viewport in the future? Right now, changing mipmap bias in a viewport affects both 2D and 3D. (Note that mipmaps are disabled by default in 2D; you need to enable them in the 2D filter property of Viewport, **and** enable the Mipmaps import option on the texture.)
> 
> This should be achievable using two viewports thanks to your PR now, but using a single viewport should reduce the performance overhead.

Should be easily doable. Basically the PR allows any class with access to MaterialStorage to create a set of samplers configured however they need it. My implementation chose to do it for each set of RenderBuffers as the mipmap bias required for rendering the scene differs depending on settings that affect the buffers, but even the same renderer pulls from different set of samplers depending on the content (e.g. shadowmaps use the version without mipmap bias despite being in a viewport with bias, as it wouldn't make much sense to use it there).
Bumping this for later, we'll most likely need this to be merged first before #81197 is as it directly affects the quality of the upscaling.

comments: This checks out with what I reported while testing [FSR 2](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/81197). That PR may have fixed the issue, I haven't checked yet.

@Calinou I specifically realized it while testing that PR.
Godot FSR 2.2 Scaling 33%
![screenshot1](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/48926464/b5f125cf-88a7-494c-b347-2116f9b538d5)
Unreal FSR 2.2 Scaling 33%
![screenshot2](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/48926464/cf254e4f-a856-4aea-a5b9-6498e151a588)
It almost looks like positive mipmap LOD bias is being applied instead of negative LOD bias.

I get the feeling it's not exactly a positive bias but rather it's not really doing anything.

I'll verify what sampler it's retrieving exactly for rendering.

Does it work after a restart?

> Note: This property is only read when the project starts. To change the mipmap LOD bias at run-time, set [Viewport.texture_mipmap_bias](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_viewport.html#class-viewport-property-texture-mipmap-bias) instead.

RenderDoc shows it's just picking the sampler with no mipmap bias.

The problem is the renderer picks the uniform bindings of the default samplers that have no bias applied.

There's a _custom_ set shared with other things, but frankly that design seems prone to problems as the viewports can't apply their own mipmap bias individually.

Perhaps material storage should be able to create samplers on demand with the bias required by the renderer.

review_comments: We need to include the project settings for ``rendering/textures/default_filters/use_nearest_mipmap_filter`` and ``rendering/textures/default_filters/anisotropic_filtering_level`` here so that they continue to apply to the default samplers

Should we query the global settings inside the allocate function then so we don't have to query the global where I moved it as well (ideally only at the top of the function and not per iteration like the previous code did)?
I think thats a good idea. There's no point in making them parameters if we always pull from the global settings
